Acclivity, meaning “an upward slope” is a nod to our vineyard site on the eastern slopes of Alexander Valley. Our plum-colored label pays homage to Tim Murphy and where it all began. Eric and Kyle met in 2013 while working at Madrona Manor in Healdsburg and quickly realized they shared the same passion for wine. After several garage vintages of trial and error, Eric and Kyle made the decision to formally start Acclivity Vineyards. They set out to make a wine of place rather than style. Acclivity pays homage to the past while utilizing modern practices and techniques. Audacieux means bold, courageous and daring and embodies our approach to crafting this Napa Valley Cabernet. We embarked on this brand with an audacious approach to create a high quality elegant European style Napa wine from the ridge top vineyards looking down on Oakville. This wine is unfiltered & aged for 24 months in new French oak. Family winemaker John Bambury is the grandson of Catherine Bonneau who first conceived of a vineyard on the family’s farmland in Sonoma. He has been spearheading all winemaking operations on behalf of the family business since 2000. His inaugural release of the 2002 Bonneau Los Carneros Chardonnay has led to more than a dozen widely acclaimed vintages in a growing array of varietals and styles – all of them carefully handcrafted by John and his team. Clayton Fritz, now president, resides on the one hundred acre plus property on a hillside location now known as the Fritz Vineyard and winery. The property boasts a unique energy efficient 3- tiered subterranean winery which enables wines to be made with the old-world technique of a gravity flow production system. The Héroe (Air-o-way, Spanish for hero) label offered by Sculpterra honors not only the vineyard workers of our family winery but pays respect to the unsung heroes of the wine industry. Throughout the region and beyond – the real heroes, the workers. Héroe wines are designed to be fruit forward and easy drinking, a great wine for any occasion. All the grapes are hand-picked from the estate vineyard and produced with just a touch of oak influence. An interesting note is that the back of every bottle has a picture of everyone that participated in that bottles harvest. Hollywood screen writer Robert Kamen considers himself an “accidental” success. In 1980, he found inspiration in 280 acres on the southwestern slopes of the Mayacomas Mountains in Sonoma. With a check from his first screen play, Robert made a commitment. Viticulturist Phil Coturri was introduced to the project and shared Roberts’s philosophy on preserving the wilderness of the site and implementing as little intervention as possible. Celebrated winemaker Mark Harold makes some of the most stunning wines from this property. As a small, family-owned winery we live our lives amidst the vines. Our vineyard and the rhythms of the season are constant reminders that the soil, the air, the water and the vines are the essence of the wines we craft. We’ve always said that great fruit is the real star of our winemaking team. So we let the grapes take center stage, patiently nurturing the vines to produce fruit with intense, ripe and balanced flavors. Then we let time, traditional winemaking techniques and good French oak work their magic. Born from a love of wine and music, La Voix explores French varietals through the sensory and emotional stimulations that are shared by both mediums. Music through performance and recording conveys a powerful, emotional expression. Likewise, through soil, vineyards, and production, wine elicits an equal effect. Both rely on dynamics and tension created by harmonizing high, medium, and low frequencies. In 1972 Ken Laird found a prune orchard in northern Napa Valley that he was able to convert to grape vines with the help of Robert Mondavi. This 70-acre vineyard was his first successful planting. Thirty years later the Laird family has become the biggest grape grower in Napa Valley. You have tasted Lairds fruit in other winery crafted wines. Being one of the biggest grape growers, the Laird Family Estate is also a custom crush facility which houses many boutique wine makers. The Laird Family wines are made from the top 1% of their favorite fruit. Maley Brothers is a small, handcraft, grower’s label, originally founded by brothers Joe and Louis Maley. Today, Joe’s son, Todd Maley, does all the farming and works with winemaker Chad Joseph on the production of Maley Brothers wines. Less than 1% of the wine grapes farmed in Maley Vineyards goes into their own wines. Byron’s philosophy is to have minimal manipulation with the fermentation of his grapes. Mithra the Sun God, the uncreated creator was the dominate religion of the Roman Empire pre-Christianity. The theme was simple; it was immortality to become one with Mithra. To gain knowledge of the heavens and to be reborn again. Of course, nothing has changed. The story and the wine are about the same. Continuity. After more than 3 decades at The Ojai Vineyard, what keeps me motivated and excited about running a winery is the craft. The slow process of assessing the outcome of choices made with experience and intuition is what it’s all about—and using that knowledge to make wines that fit a harmonious vision. Keeping the place small, and keeping my hands in the winemaking has allowed me to stay focused on craft.
